title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
abstract: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis, and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological, and human health studies. Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models─including both endogenous and synthetic molecules─to enable their study across diverse targets…
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Highly Tunable Metal-Peptide Piezoelectrics for Tissue Regeneration
abstract: Piezoelectricity, first discovered in 1880, has been dominated by inorganic materials, whose strong electromechanical responses typically arise from achiral, noncentrosymmetric crystal structures and highly polar bonds. However, their brittleness and poor biosafety, biocompatibility and biodegradability under physiological conditions severely limit biomedical applications and clinical translation. Here we report a general design strategy for constructing a distinct class of highly tunable metal-peptide piezoelectrics that enable efficient tissue repair and regeneration.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A robotics- and machine learning-integrated workflow for discovering all-natural plastic substitutes.
abstract: The global accumulation of nondegradable petrochemical plastic waste is driving the search for biodegradable substitutes derived from natural resources. However, discovering all-natural composite materials that match the optical, thermal and mechanical performance of commercial plastics remains challenging because traditional iterative optimization is inefficient. Here the workflow described in this Protocol accelerates the screening process by using automated robotics for liquid handing and machine learning to predict material properties.

title: Guided Serendipity: A Materials Chemistry Framework for the Discovery of Durable Inorganic Pigments
abstract: Inorganic pigments are still found mainly by experiment and good luck, even though solid-state chemistry can now explain the color of almost every pigment we know. Explaining a color, however, is not the same as designing one. The requirements for a useful pigment are often in tension: it must absorb visible light strongly and selectively, yet also remain chemically and thermally stable and free of toxic elements.

title: Regulating Functionalized MXene Crystal-Field Splitting toward Efficient Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis of Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
abstract: MXenes offer fast conductive frameworks with abundant intrinsic active metal sites, making them promising cathode catalysts for lithium–oxygen batteries for addressing sluggish oxygen kinetics and severe cathode passivation. However, the predictive electronic descriptors for rationally regulating these intrinsic active sites remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of crystal-field splitting engineering at Ti sites of Ti3C2-MXene to achieve bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Long-term study reveals how humidity affects the durability of biodegradable thermoplastic polymers
abstract: As the demand for sustainable alternatives to conventional plastics continues to grow, biodegradable polymers such as poly(lactic acid) (PLA) are attracting increasing attention for applications ranging from packaging to consumer products.

title: Correlation Length-Scale Control in High-Precision Born–Oppenheimer Calculations of He2+
abstract: We present a variational framework for high-precision Born–Oppenheimer calculations and apply it to the electronic ground state of the helium molecular ion, He2+. To obtain uniform accuracy from the short-range well to the dissociation limit, the variational expansion combines fully correlated molecular ECG basis functions with a frozen asymptotic monomer–pair sector optimized in the noninteracting limit. This sector stabilizes the variational optimization at large internuclear separations, where the interaction energy becomes much smaller than the monomer contributions. The resulting BO potential converges to subppb relative numerical accuracy across the entire range and provides a reliable foundation for high-precision rovibrational calculations. In particular, nonrelativistic dissociation energies are obtained with estimated uncertainties of the order of 10–4 cm–1. Although developed here for He2+ within an ECG framework, the approach should also be applicable to larger molecular systems with weak interfragment interactions.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Team maximizes efficiency of heavy rare-earth elements for high-performance permanent magnets
abstract: Neodymium–iron–boron (Nd–Fe–B) permanent magnets are key components in electric vehicle traction motors and wind turbines. In particular, heavy rare-earth elements, which are added to maintain coercivity (resistance to demagnetization) even at high temperatures, are extremely expensive and have unstable supply chains, consequently placing a significant burden on industry. Since completely eliminating heavy rare-earth elements remains difficult, the most important technical challenge is to minimize their use while maintaining magnetic performance.

title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
abstract: Chemically defined organic heterobilayers offer a route to programmable interfacial coupling, yet their on-surface construction remains challenging due to the instability of dynamic covalent frameworks during sequential growth. Here, we report a guest-induced COF-on-COF growth strategy that enables deterministic heteroepitaxy of imine/boroxine covalent organic framework (COF) heterobilayers at solid–liquid interfaces.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Symmetry-reduced k-point sampling and Wannier analysis with localized Gaussian orbitals
abstract: Brillouin-zone sampling with localized orbitals requires consistent transformations between sparse real-space matrices and complex Bloch states. Symmetry reduces the number of reciprocal-space problems, but scalar integration weights alone cannot reconstruct the matrices and wavefunctions needed for densities and orbital analysis. We develop a unified formulation of these transformations for nonorthogonal Gaussian bases and describe its implementation in CP2K. Atom permutations, local orbital rotations, and lattice phases connect irreducible-point solutions to full symmetry orbits while preserving the overlap metric. Direct and fast lattice transforms couple this construction to self-consistent calculations, including complex orbital optimization and finite-temperature occupations. Gauge-consistent full-mesh orbitals and directed inter-point overlaps support Wannier90 export, Wannier construction, and Hamiltonian interpolation. In silicon and aluminium tests, symmetry reduces a 64-point mesh to four representatives while retaining cell energies or electronic free energies within $1.5\times10^{-12}$ hartree of the unreduced calculation. Hybrid exchange and many-body applications illustrate the additional role of auxiliary bases and transfer momenta. The resulting framework connects symmetry-reduced integration to gauge-consistent analysis of periodic electronic states within a localized-orbital representation.

title: Magnon-Phonon-Polariton Optomechanics in a van der Waals Magnet
abstract: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

title: When Does Discrete Ricci Curvature Help? An Edge-Level Analysis of Curvature-Enhanced GCNs for PPI Prediction
abstract: Curvature-enhanced graph convolutional networks (CGCN) incorporate Ollivier-Ricci curvature (ORC), grounded in optimal transport theory, into message passing, motivated by the claim that curvature-weighted edges alleviate "over-squashing" at structural bottlenecks. But does CGCN's improvement actually come from mitigating over-squashing? We investigate this on four real-world protein-protein interaction (PPI) datasets, comparing CGCN against a standard GCN at the level of individual edges rather than aggregate metrics alone. While CGCN improves aggregate AUC, AUPR, and F1 across all four datasets, this gain is concentrated almost entirely on low-degree edges, while performance on low-curvature (bottleneck) edges systematically degrades in three of four datasets, the opposite of what the over-squashing motivation predicts. Examining the learned edge-weight function directly, together with clustering-validity metrics, edge-distance ratios, and a layer-depth ablation across four depths, we find evidence for an alternative account: curvature-weighting sharpens the separation between clusters, which improves intra-cluster predictions at the cost of inter-cluster (bottleneck) ones. We test this account against topologically defined communities rather than the classification labels used elsewhere. Additionally, we offer practical guidance on when to prefer CGCN over standard GCN, depending on whether intra- or inter-cluster predictions matter most.

title: tmol: a GPU-accelerated implementation of the Rosetta energy function for machine learning
abstract: Physics-inspired forcefields complement generative machine learning models, showing better generalization beyond the training distribution. However, these forcefields are typically slow to evaluate, and their derivatives are difficult to integrate into ML frameworks. We introduce tmol, a GPU-native PyTorch library implementing the state-of-the-art RosettaGenFF forcefield. tmol supports efficient batched differentiable scoring and whole-structure refinement with up to 362-fold throughput increase (batched). Used as a reward in generative protein design, tmol increases hydrogen bonds and water bridges at designed interfaces.

title: A bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an aromatic cyclopentadienide ring
abstract: Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, but are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Now a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide ring has been prepared and found to exhibit unusual structural and electronic properties, enabling site-selective reactivity on its π surface for both covalent functionalization and metal coordination.

title: Integrating Mouse Transcriptomics and Human Multi-Cohort Data Reveals an Inflammatory Gene Signature Mediating Jaceosidin's Therapeutic Effect in Ulcerative Colitis.
abstract: Jaceosidin exerts protective effects against ulcerative colitis (UC), but its molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study integrates transcriptomics, machine learning, and co-expression network analysis to elucidate Jaceosidin's targets in UC. A dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse colitis model with transcriptome sequencing was established. Core genes were identified by WGCNA and cross-dataset analysis of public UC datasets. Three machine learning algorithms constructed a risk prediction model. GO/KEGG, GSEA, immune infiltration, and single-cell analyses were performed.

title: Time-Resolved SAXS Unveils Two Structurally Distinct Membranes upon Cytochrome c Binding
abstract: The association of peripheral proteins with lipid membranes can couple lateral lipid organization to interbilayer correlations, but the temporal evolution of these structural changes remains difficult to characterize experimentally. Here, we use time-resolved small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) to investigate the structural evolution of POPC:POPG large unilamellar vesicles following the addition of cytochrome~c. The experimental profiles are analyzed globally using an extension of the SASBIN model incorporating molecularly constrained bilayer electron-density profiles, lateral lipid inhomogeneities, and interbilayer correlations. A two-population description consistently reproduces the SAXS profiles, with distinct structural contributions associated with protein-free and cytochrome-c-associated bilayers. Within this framework, the protein-associated population exhibits lateral correlations consistent with POPG-rich domains and a progressive increase in lamellar ordering, whereas the protein-free population is characterized by molecular-scale effective inhomogeneities. The fitted time-dependent parameters suggest that population redistribution and lateral reorganization are most pronounced during the early stages of the interaction, while some parameters describing interbilayer correlations evolve more gradually. These results provide a quantitative structural description of how cytochrome~c association can couple lateral lipid organization and lamellar ordering in mixed zwitterionic/anionic membranes.

title: Deep-Learning Prediction of Reversed-Phase Liquid Chromatographic Retention Times for Small Molecules and Pharmaceuticals: A Systematic Review
abstract: Predicted retention times can narrow candidate lists in liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC–HRMS). Deep-learning models report errors near the variability between repeated measurements, but their credibility depends on the evaluation design. We reviewed deep-learning retention-time prediction for non-polymeric small molecules in reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RP-LC). Searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through August 3, 2026, identified 594 records; 33 studies were eligible.

title: As a beekeeping pesticide fails, the industry scrambles to adapt
abstract: Parasitic mites have evolved resistance to the pesticide amitraz, but only a few are searching for alternatives

title: Accelerating auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo with mixed-precision random propagators
abstract: We develop an algorithm to propagate auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) wavefunctions in mixed precision. We target NVIDIA Tensor Cores using the TensorFloat-32 (TF32) format. We approximate each full-precision array by a TF32 leading term and a TF32 residual, and each full-precision matrix product by three TF32 products accumulated in full precision. Benchmarks on hydrogen chains show that mixed-precision propagation is consistently faster than double-precision GPU propagation, with an increasing advantage as the system size grows. The resulting local-energy deviations remain small over the propagation windows considered here. These results identify the stochastic two-body propagator as a particularly effective target for reduced precision, while our method allows higher precision to be retained for accuracy-sensitive operations. Hence, our algorithm provides a practical way to speed up AFQMC calculations and demonstrates where reduced precision can be applied without adverse effects on the method's accuracy.

title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
abstract: Predicting the effects of genetic perturbations requires models that generalize beyond observed cell contexts and gene combinations. We introduce Occam, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) framework for representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction. Occam combines cell representations learned through denoising with gene interaction, text, and protein-sequence features. It achieves the highest aggregate representation scores for perturbation information and cell-type preservation with batch integration. In cross-context few-shot prediction, a perturbation and a cell context are each observed during training, but never together. Occam better captures the measured response patterns for these unobserved combinations than four retrained competitors or direct transfer of the same perturbation's measured effects from other training cell lines. Without fine-tuning, Occam best distinguishes perturbations among the evaluated models and simple baselines in cell lines held out from predictor training, across seen and unseen assays. Predicting expression levels accurately in these settings remains challenging. For double perturbations, which target two genes simultaneously, Occam composes learned single-gene responses to better capture the combined response and reduce expression error compared with competing models and summed single-gene effects. These gains extend to both strongly additive and weakly additive responses. Together, these results support simple MLPs for cell representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction across contexts and gene combinations.

title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. We develop a rigorous checkpointing system that enables highly capable audit agents, a scalable form of oversight for agentic research. Audit agents autonomously identify errors at higher rates than previous AI scientist agents, and scientists collaborating with audit agents identify 14x more valid errors versus scientists performing manual review. In three case studies led by domain experts across physical science, social science, and life science, we developed a multimodal photometric-redshift estimator that resolves complementary failures of images and photometry, achieving 0.971 AUROC for low-redshift classification; documented an 83% rise in Florida homeowners-insurance premiums from 2013 to 2023, with a growing, regressive burden; and identified CD4+ T-cell relay genes, which both receive and exert broad transcriptional regulation, enriched for autoimmune disease associations. Together, these results show how autonomous research can expand scientists' empirical reach while centering their authority over research direction and their ability to understand and challenge the evidence.

title: Sparse Integer Fourier Transform and Its Application In Machine Learning
abstract: The Discrete Fourier transform, mainly implemented by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), has been essential for numerous domains, such as digital signal processing and feature extraction in materials design. However, current FFT methods suffer from extensive non-trivial multiplications and twiddle-factor operations in the big data era. To improve the computational efficiency of FFT, this study proposes Sparse Integer Fourier Transform (SIFT), a method that leverages the fast computing of sparsity and small integers, and applies the Radix-n method to derive an FFT. The 2N-point DFT matrix in Radix-n FFT is decomposed into four sparse integer matrices. A diagonal matrix containing complex twiddle factors is efficiently approximated using an optimization strategy while the remaining matrices retain sparsity and integer entries. For radix-32 FFT, SIFT reduces the estimated arithmetic cost by 75%, with RMSE below $2.3765\times10^{-8}$ and MAPE below 0.01089%. We evaluate frequency extraction in a numerical test and an engineering case. In the numerical test, MAPE and RMSE are below 2.016% and $2.536\times10^{-6}$, respectively. For wind turbine fault diagnosis, SIFT extracts compact spectral features that retain fault information while reducing the classifier's input dimensionality relative to the full time series.

title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
abstract: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking. Given 50 demonstrations for each task, ALOHA Lightning autonomously completes bimanual tasks such as ball tossing and catching, folding shorts, battery insertion, and bussing tables for over 80% success rates while close to human speed. Project website: https://flash-aloha.github.io/

title: quantEM: Quantitative Electron Microscopy Analysis from Differentiable Physics to Neural Priors
abstract: Quantitative electron microscopy includes imaging, diffraction, spectroscopy, and tomography measurements, and the analysis of these measurements increasingly requires solving inverse problems with physical forward models. Open-source software has made many of these analyses widely available, but most packages are organized around a single modality, so that multimodal analyses require moving data between packages, and new methods cannot easily reuse the physical models and optimizers of existing ones. Here we present quantEM, an open-source Python package for quantitative electron microscopy that uses PyTorch tensors for computation and automatic differentiation, and Zarr for storage. We implement each analysis method by writing a differentiable forward model and choosing a representation, loss function, constraints, and optimizer from a library of components, so that every method runs on CPUs and GPUs, can be saved and resumed, and uses the same calibrated data structures and visualization tools. We describe the current modules, including orientation and strain mapping, direct and iterative ptychography, tomography with neural representations, and X-ray and electron energy-loss spectroscopy, and show how we assemble combined methods such as ptychographic tomography from existing components. quantEM is available under the MIT license, together with documentation, tutorials, and curated example datasets.

title: Dynamics and transport in LiF using classical and machine learned interatomic potentials
abstract: We perform molecular dynamics simulations of molten Lithium Fluoride, comparing the classical Buckingham and Born-Huggins-Mayer potentials with machine-learnt interatomic potentials - the MACE-MP-0b3 (small) foundation model potential, and a fine-tuned version thereof. We find that the MACE-MP-0b3, out-of-the-box, is able to accurately reproduce the experimental shear viscosity across the liquid state comparable with polarisable potentials despite not itself being polarisable. Previous viscosities computed using classical potentials are under-predicted, which has previously been attributed to a suppressed melting temperature. Prompted by this we compare the melting points of these potentials. We find that the machine-learnt potentials address the significant underestimation of the melting point of the classical potentials, though the refined potential and the foundation model differ significantly between themselves. We probe the microscopic structure and dynamics of each model to further elucidate the considerable change in viscosity between classical and machine-learnt potentials. We find that, despite their lower melting temperature, classical potentials produce considerably stiffer, higher frequency, single-particle and collective charge-transport dynamics on account of their fixed charges. However, in the long-wavelength limit, the many-body machine-learnt potentials feature more elastic collective motion that governs the diffusion of momentum and is therefore responsible for the enhanced shear viscosity.

title: Optical characterization of Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride
abstract: Amorphous silicon nitride is the leading low-loss, CMOS-compatible platform for wafer-scale integrated photonics. Encapsulating transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers within this platform offers a promising route towards scalable TMD-photonic circuits. Yet the effect of this amorphous dielectric on the optical response of the monolayer remains poorly understood. Here, we compare monolayer MoSe$_2$ encapsulated in amorphous silicon nitride with a hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated reference, using differential reflectivity and photoluminescence. Whereas the reference is dominated by the neutral exciton, the nitride-encapsulated monolayer shows attractive and repulsive polaron resonances separated by ${\sim}31$~meV, with emission dominated by the attractive branch. A quantitative comparison of temperature-dependent reflectance with a microscopic finite-temperature Fermi-polaron theory shows that the nitride induces substantial electron doping in the monolayer, with an electron density of $(0.8$--$0.9)\times10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$. Using the extracted density and trion binding energy as the only input parameters, the theory reproduces the photoluminescence spectra up to ${\sim}80$ K in excellent quantitative agreement with experiments, thus corroborating the Fermi-polaron description of the observed excitonic response.

title: Bandwidth-tunable thermal emitter via dynamic resonator coupling and loss
abstract: We demonstrate a dynamically tunable omnidirectional thermal emitter that can be switched from a narrowband emission state to a broadband state. The structure is a metal-backed multilayer with subwavelength thickness across the mid-infrared, which forms an angle-insensitive (up to 60°) optical cavity with one input port. We used an ultrathin VO2 layer to dynamically switch the coupling and loss coefficients of this optical cavity, resulting in narrowband emission from the vibrational mode of a polar dielectric layer that is part of the multilayer stack when the VO2 is in its insulating phase, and broadband emission from a nearly impedance-matched cavity when the VO2 is switched to its lossy metallic phase. We fabricated the structure around a free-standing silicon membrane and integrated it onto a printed circuit board (PCB), which enabled electrical switching of the emitter at the ten-to-hundred millisecond scale, and can be used for free-space identification, tagging, or communication.

title: Quantifying dark modes to advance polariton chemistry
abstract: Researchers have resolved a long-standing paradox in polariton chemistry—a field that explores how to control chemical reactions by trapping molecules inside optical cavities where light and matter strongly interact (known as strong coupling). Previously, a major theoretical hurdle stood in the way: Calculations indicated that millions of inactive molecular states—known as dark modes—should greatly outnumber active polaritons, making it seemingly impossible for light-matter coupling to influence chemistry.

title: Carboxymethyl cellulose-regulated poly(vinyl alcohol) ionic networks for recyclable strain sensing.
abstract: Conductive hydrogels are promising soft materials for flexible sensing, electronic skins, and human-machine interaction; however, integrating mechanical robustness, stable ionic transport, environmental adaptability, and reprocessability within a fully physically crosslinked network remains challenging. Here, we report a Hofmeister-effect-assisted multi-interaction strategy for constructing a physically crosslinked ionic hydrogel based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), termed P-MC.

title: When Electrolytes Become Dopants: Programming Charge Transport in Conductive Metal−Organic Framework Transistors
abstract: Conjugated metal−organic frameworks (c-MOFs) operating in ionic environments have emerged as promising microporous and conductive systems for next-generation applications. Understanding the interplay between electrolyte composition and electronic−ionic mixed transport remains a critical barrier to the rational design of novel devices. Here, we demonstrate that electrolyte composition provides a direct and programmable handle for controlling charge transport and field-effect properties in c-MOF electrochemical transistors (ECTs). Two types of c-MOF thin films composed of the conjugated linker 2,3,5,6,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and either Cu2+ or Ni2+ ions, namely, Cu3(HHTP)2 and Ni3(HHTP)2, were employed as transistor channel materials. Using these c-MOFs as prototypical conductive frameworks, we systematically interrogate the influence of ionic strength, ion identity, pH, and gate configuration on transistor operation. Across these variables, we unveil robust and quantitative relationships linking the nature and conditions of the electrolyte to variations in charge neutrality, modulation of transconductance, and transitions between transport regimes. For instance, increasing ionic strength shifts the transfer curves of Cu3(HHTP)2- and Ni3(HHTP)2-based ECTs toward a more negative potential, with a linear dependence on the logarithm of ion concentration. The ion-hydrated radius strongly influences ion-electron transport, as smaller cations more readily permeate the framework and reduce surface potential. Charge neutrality point potential (VCNP) displays a linear pH dependence, with sensitivities comparable to conducting polymer ECTs. Device performance is also influenced by the gate electrode configuration (liquid-junction or pseudo-reference electrodes). Extensive field-effect characterization demonstrates good electrochemical stability. A unified mechanistic model successfully describes the coupled ionic−electronic transport governing c-MOF device operation.

title: Machine learning for small-molecule antibiotics - discovery to pre-clinical optimization
abstract: BackgroundThe rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health crisis, with 4.71 million associated deaths and 1.14 million attributable deaths in 2021. By 2050, these tolls are forecasted to rise to 8.22 million associated deaths and 1.91 million attributable deaths annually. Despite this growing burden, the antibacterial pipeline is alarmingly lean, with few candidates exhibiting truly novel mechanisms of action (MOA).
venue: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

title: Metal-based engineered nanoparticles and aquatic phototrophic microorganisms: From single-species to natural communities interactions
abstract: The widespread use of metal-based engineered nanoparticles (ENPs) has led to their release into aquatic environments, raising concerns about their potential environmental impact. Despite considerable research to understand the influence of ENPs on phototrophic microorganisms under laboratory settings, their influences on natural communities remain poorly understood, and this gap has not yet been comprehensively reviewed. By integrating the current knowledge across laboratory and field studies, this review critically examines how the effect of ENPs on phototrophic microorganisms propagate across ecological scales, from individual organisms to natural communities. ENPs toxicity towards phototrophic microorganisms depends on water physico-chemical characteristics and intrinsic properties of ENPs. Cellular traits and taxonomic identities strongly influence ENPs toxicity, with smaller cells and cyanobacteria being more prone to adverse effects than large species and other taxa. The selective toxicity of ENPs can reshape natural communities without necessarily reducing their total biomass. This may result in the dominance of opportunistic species, decreasing species diversity and making communities more vulnerable to environmental disturbances. Consequently, ENPs may trigger cascading effects on biogeochemical cycles and food webs, that could be further intensified by climate change. This review further identifies critical methodological limitations in assessing the sensitivity of natural communities to ENPs and emphasises the importance of using recent analytical techniques, such as single-cell techniques, machine learning and omics techniques, to overcome these challenges. Improving our understanding of ENPs toxicity towards natural communities is therefore essential for accurately assessing their ecological risk assessment.

title: Probing Metal-Organic Framework Stoichiometry Using Quantitative NMR and TGA
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks do not always have perfect stoichiometry because of defects, modulators, or mixed linkers. A common approach to quantify these defects is to define a value for ‘missing linkers’, typically by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). In this approach, the researcher must isolate the mass loss attributable to the linker and make a priori assumptions about the material composition.

title: A multiscale modeling - experimental framework reveals the interplay between drivers of Drosophila wing morphogenesis
abstract: Robust organ formation depends on the coordinated regulation of cellular mechanics, yet how mechanobiological processes such as controlled cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion, actomyosin contractility, membrane stiffness, and internal pressure interlink to generate an organ's architecture remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigated underlying mechanobiology principles using Drosophila wing disc eversion, the metamorphic conversion of a larval epithelial sac into a functional wing.

title: 3D Gaussian splatting for forensic autopsy documentation: Influence of image acquisition strategy on reconstruction quality.
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) documentation is an integral part of recording postmortem findings and reconstructing crime scenes. While photogrammetry is well established in forensic routine practice, deep learning-based view synthesis has introduced 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) as a promising technique for fast and photorealistic 3D reconstruction. However, its applicability and robustness in forensic autopsy documentation have not yet been systematically investigated. Ten forensic autopsy cases were documented using a standardized, flash-based photogrammetric workflow and reconstructed using 3DGS.

title: Observing interstitial hydrogen in alloys
abstract: New approach could help researchers understand metal embrittlement caused by hydrogen

title: Discovery of cell-permeable inhibitors for human succinyl-CoA:glutarate-CoA transferase
abstract: Glutaric Aciduria Type I (GA-1) is a recessive, serious neurometabolic disorder characterized by a build-up of toxic metabolites in the lysine metabolic pathway with no current pharmacological treatment. Previous mouse studies have shown that a deficiency in SUGCT attenuates the accumulation of some of these metabolites in vivo. These results highlight the potential for SUGCT as a therapeutic target in treating GA-1. We had previously identified biochemical inhibitors for SUGCT and had solved the crystal structure of the protein, both apo and bound to an inhibitor. However, we were unable to demonstrate cellular activity for these compounds. In this study, we report findings from additional in vitro high-throughput screening and address these challenges by developing an improved cell-based assay to detect SUGCT inhibition. We show that by improving the permeability of valsartan using its ethyl ester prodrug, SUGCT is effectively inhibited in GA-1 cells. We also identify meclofenamic acid as a new SUGCT inhibitor with cellular activity, providing additional validation and highlighting this enzyme target potential for GA-1.

title: How Elasticity and Chiral Damping Shape Domain-Wall Creep
abstract: Asymmetric domain-wall expansion in the creep regime provides an experimentally accessible probe of the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) and, in principle, chiral damping. However, severe discrepancies with complementary measurement techniques and the lack of a model describing the full experimental phenomenology of the creep of chiral domain walls, limits the application of these measurements. Here, using a symmetry decomposition of the velocity curve, we derive an analytical model describing the coupled influence of domain-wall stiffness and chiral damping in the creep regime. Their interplay generates the antisymmetric distortion that shifts the velocity minimum away from the DMI field. Applied to Co-based magnetic multilayers, the model yields iDMI values consistent with BLS and flow-regime benchmarks and identifies the reasons for the longstanding discrepancy. The model provides insights for possible strategies to measure chiral damping via creep dynamics of domain walls.

title: Model-free stiffness measurement of microscale soft contacts by far-field traction force microscopy
abstract: The microscale stiffness of soft materials governs their contact mechanics, adhesion and friction, yet it is surprisingly difficult to measure. Micro or nanoindentation is typically used, but extracting stiffness from these measurements requires using contact mechanics models (e.g. JKR), whose assumptions often break down for soft adhesive contacts. Here, we introduce far-field traction force microscopy (FF-TFM) to extract stiffness without using any contact model. We drag a colloidal probe mounted on an atomic-force microscope across a soft surface, measuring the friction force while imaging the displacements of fluorescent tracers on the substrate. Far from the contact, in the elastic limit, these lateral displacements depend solely on the friction force and the substrate stiffness, and fitting them with the point-force solution thus gives the substrate's Young's modulus directly. We successfully match bulk rheology moduli with FF-TFM for six different silicone elastomers, where JKR fits to indentation data underestimate moduli by as much as 40\% of their bulk values. Our approach also enables tracking how the probe slips across the surface. We find that soft contacts can "pre-slip" with no detectable signature in the force signal, unlike stiffer contacts. FF-TFM thus offers a contact-model-free route to measuring microscale stiffness and slip behavior in soft materials.

title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring
abstract: Long-term wearable electrophysiological recording systems are essential for both clinical and real-world environments. While a wide range of wearable devices have been reported for electrocardiogram (ECG) and electromyogram (EMG) recording applications, most electroencephalography (EEG) measurements still require subjects to remain stationary while wearing rigid and uncomfortable equipment. Here, a soft and wearable sponge pillar EEG electrode is presented for long-term and motion-tolerant EEG recording. The electrode is composed of two layers of a carbon black (CB)-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite, where a firmer solid base assists in bypassing hair, enabling stable access to the scalp, while a porous sponge tip ensures comfort, reliable contact, and low skin-electrode impedance. Fabricated via a sugar templating process without microfabrication steps, the microporous sponge structure offers low modulus and significantly enhances the contact area with the skin when loaded with conductive gel. This allows the electrode to achieve a lower contact impedance of $1.62 \times 10^{4}\,Ω$ at 10 Hz, outperforming conventional gelled electrodes while maintaining gel stability for over 18 hours. With the electrodes integrated into wearable form factors such as headbands, headphones, and baseball caps, EEG signal recording during motion have been demonstrated, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 16.46 dB. These features establish the sponge pillar electrode as a promising platform for next generation wearable EEG systems, enabling comfortable, stable, and prolonged brain signal acquisition on ambulatory subjects and in naturalistic environments.

title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
abstract: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction. Calpha aims at one general model that folds proteins and complexes, understands protein sequence and structure, and lets its language reasoning influence the structures it predicts. This report covers the first step, in which an LLM outputs single-chain protein structures. Qwen3.5-9B reads a sequence enriched with ESM2 residue features. It can respond in text or emit a token that invokes a pretrained SimpleFold structure head, which receives information about the protein only through Qwen's residue states. Under a fixed folding request, the head achieves mean TM-scores of 0.808 on the FoldBench-334 development set, 0.635 on CASP16 domains and 0.900 on a CAMEO-style PDB set. We compare these predictions with a baseline in which ESM2-3B encodes the sequence and a fine-tuned SimpleFold-3B head predicts the coordinates. The two systems also differ in trainable weights, training duration and crop length. For chains of 100--299 residues, all three paired confidence intervals include zero. At 300--600 residues, the mean differences are -0.044, -0.160 and -0.025, respectively. In a separate test, four English request types triggered folding on every evaluated example. Protein training reduced accuracy on a 350-item MMLU-Pro subset from 77.4% to 70.3%. An LLM can therefore output single-chain structures from its own states, with lower long-chain scores in the current comparisons and reduced accuracy on the evaluated MMLU-Pro subset. Complex prediction, structure understanding and the effect of language reasoning on the predicted coordinates remain future work.

title: A tunable multi-gated platform for superlattice engineering in bilayer graphene
abstract: Periodic potentials with length scales much larger than crystal lattice constants can generate low-energy electronic minibands. While small-angle twisted van der Waals heterostructures have been widely used to realize such physics, correlated phases are often limited by twist-angle inhomogeneity, strain, and disorder. Here, we investigate high-quality Bernal bilayer graphene placed on a patterned graphite gate, featuring a triangular array of holes, forming a new class of "gate-engineered" superlattices tunable through three independent electrostatic gates. Near the charge neutrality point, we observe insulating states characteristic of miniband formation. Temperature-dependent transport reveals activated gaps consistent with theory, and Hall measurements indicate charge-carrier inversion. Notably, the superlattice can be reconfigured electrostatically using various gate combinations, enabling flexible band-structure design without mechanical twisting. The results highlight a new route to band engineering, potentially extendable to complex periodic structures that are untenable in natural materials.

title: How PFAS Could Disrupt the Thyroid
Communication-Efficient Hamiltonian Evaluation for Massively Parallel Tensor-Product Bitstring Selected Configuration Interaction
abstract: Extreme-scale selected configuration interaction (SCI) requires coordinated Hamiltonian evaluation, distributed CI-vector storage, and interprocess communication on massively parallel computers. Our previous work [J. Chem. Phys. 164, 194103 (2026)] introduced the tensor-product bitstring selected configuration interaction (TBSCI) framework, combining on-the-fly Hamiltonian evaluation with fully distributed CI-vector storage and enabling parallel diagonalization of trillion-determinant spaces on up to 54,000 Fugaku nodes. Here, we introduce FLIP, a new Hamiltonian evaluation algorithm within TBSCI that reorganizes the CI-vector layout and excitation-link data to replace remote CI-coefficient transfers for $α$-electron double excitations with local coefficient access and link retrieval from nearby MPI ranks. In communication-intensive full configuration interaction (FCI) benchmarks on Fugaku, no exposed communication waiting time was recorded on the slowest process across all 32 measured Hamiltonian-vector multiplications. For N$_2$/cc-pVTZ with $2.62\times10^{12}$ determinants, the multiplication achieved 91.3% strong-scaling efficiency from 18,000 to 81,000 nodes (more than 3.8 million compute cores). We also obtained an FCI reference potential-energy curve for N$_2$/cc-pVTZ. At all six bond lengths, spin bitstrings selected by their collective weights in reference SCI wavefunctions yielded variational TBSCI energies within 0.1 m$E_h$ of FCI using fewer than 1% of the FCI determinants, demonstrating the compactness of the tensor-product bitstring representation. Finally, we discuss local construction of double-excitation links to substantially reduce communication volume and eliminate persistent storage of precomputed double-link tables for future second-order perturbation theory calculations with large external determinant spaces.

title: Solubility and Diffusion of Hydrogen Isotopes and Helium in Molten FLiBe
abstract: Tritium produced in molten 2LiF-BeF$_2$ (FLiBe) may dissolve as T$_2$ or as TF, which differ greatly in solubility. Permeation experiments give a solubility close to that of HF and a flux proportional to the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which has usually been taken as evidence of dissociation. We have developed a fixed-charge classical potential for FLiBe containing atomic tritium, T$_2$, TF, the hydride ion T$^-$ and helium, fitted only to periodic DFT calculations for hydrogen. The nuclei are classical, so the solubilities apply to all hydrogen isotopes. The host reproduces the measured density and neutron structure factor but is too fluid close to the liquidus. The calculated solubilities of T$_2$ and TF agree with experiment, and neither molecule dissociates in the melt. Because TF is much more soluble, it holds most of the dissolved tritium unless the salt is strongly reducing, and at constant redox potential its concentration varies with the square root of the T$_2$ pressure, which accounts for the permeation results without dissociation. Helium does not change the solubility of T$_2$: a helium bubble in the melt takes up T$_2$ as its Henry constant predicts, while TF is enriched at the bubble surface. T$_2$ diffuses somewhat faster than measured, and TF and T$^-$ two to three times more slowly than T$_2$.

title: artist: A Python package for differentiable ray tracing and gradient-based optimization of solar tower power plant operation
abstract: Solar tower power plants provide dispatchable, renewable energy by concentrating sunlight with thousands of mirrors, called heliostats, onto a central receiver. Efficient operation requires accurate modeling of the optical path from each heliostat to the receiver and compensation for manufacturing imperfections, kinematic misalignment, and material degradation that distort the flux distribution. Conventional ray tracers predict the flux from an assumed plant model but are limited to forward simulation. They cannot recover unknown plant parameters from measured flux nor directly optimize plant operation. We present artist, an open-source, FAIR4RS-compliant Python package implementing a fully differentiable digital twin of solar tower power plants. By making the optical pipeline, comprising heliostat surface representation, kinematics, blocking, and ray tracing, end to end differentiable, artist turns the digital twin from a passive forward model into an active physics-based tool for inverse modeling and data-driven optimization. The resulting gradient-based framework unifies tasks usually handled by separate solutions, such as reconstructing heliostat surfaces and kinematics from operational flux images without costly deflectometry, predicting irradiance at the receiver, and optimizing aim points to realize a desired receiver flux density distribution. Built on PyTorch, artist scales to real plants through GPU acceleration, a structure-of-arrays memory layout, and nested data parallelism. It interfaces with open data sources such as the PAINT database. We describe the software architecture, physical models, and optimization framework, and demonstrate the workflow on representative tasks. By integrating modeling, prediction, and optimization into a single open, interpretable package, artist provides a principled foundation for data-driven research toward autonomous solar tower operation.

title: MolReps: Taking SELFIES, Making SMILES, Teaching LLMs
abstract: The same molecule can be expressed in multiple, syntactically distinct representations, yet it remains unclear whether large language models (LLMs) can recognize and relate these equivalent encodings. We introduce MolReps, a pipeline that generates 9,600 question-answer pairs across ten representations for conversion, normalization, and 2D structure recognition. Post-training on MolReps improves text-only and multimodal models, MolQwen3-4B-Instruct (MQ3-4B-I) and MolQwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (MQ3-VL-4B-I), from $4.01\%$ to $75.13\%$ and from $7.11\%$ to $73.14\%$ (InChIKey match) on the molecule-overlap test set, respectively. On the molecule-disjoint test set, post-training increased validity from $20.35\%$ to $58.12\%$ for MQ3-4B-I and from $17.19\%$ to $59.34\%$ for MQ3-VL-4B-I. However, InChIKey match remained low, decreasing from $3.86\%$ to $3.09\%$ and from $6.44\%$ to $2.29\%$, respectively. Furthermore, the resulting models achieve a relative $27.84\%$ improvement in average over their base model on MolRepBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating molecular property prediction. These results show the effectiveness of targeted post-training for enhancing molecular representation understanding and its potential to improve downstream molecular tasks.

title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning identify macrophage RPS26 as a potential biomarker for atrial fibrillation.
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent arrhythmia worldwide, with its incidence and burden rising steeply with advancing age. However, the pathological process of AF remains incompletely understood, and the discovery of reliable biomarkers to guide gene and cell therapy remains challenging in precision medicine. This study aimed to identify potential key pathological factors in AF through an integrative single-cell and machine learning framework.

title: Copper-Catalyzed α-C–H Cyanation of Amides via Sequential Electron Transfer/Hydrogen Atom Transfer (ET/HAT)
abstract: Cyanated amides, α-cyano amides and α-amino nitriles, are highly desirable motifs and valuable synthons owing to their important roles in chemical synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Conventional approaches to these compounds typically rely on the nucleophilic attack of cyanide on imines (iminium ions) or on radical transformations from prefunctionalized alkyl halides, respectively. Herein, we report a ligand-free, copper-catalyzed cyanation reaction that enables the preparation of both classes of compounds via direct C−H functionalization without light.

title: Persistence revisited: Partitioning rather than media-specific reactivity dominates persistence in the environment
abstract: Current regulation identifies environmentally persistent chemicals often using thresholds defined for single-media half-lives. This approach ignores the large and even dominating impact of multimedia partitioning on the (bio)availability of compounds that undergo degradation, and accordingly may underestimate the chemical lifetimes by orders of magnitude. This is demonstrated through comparing chemical half-lives in water with overall persistence (Pov) in terms of environmental lifetimes calculated through a steady-state multimedia mass-balance model.

title: The secret to building Moon bases may be hiding in emergency blankets
abstract: Scientists have turned the thin plastic used in emergency blankets into remarkably strong insulation that could help astronauts survive the Moon's extreme temperatures. Built from hundreds of stacked layers, the material withstands crushing pressure without losing its thermal protection, potentially paving the way for tougher, longer-lasting lunar habitats.

title: Shared characteristics establish Corynebacterium glutamicum ClpCP1P2 as a tractable model for mycobacterial orthologs
abstract: Clp proteases are central to bacterial proteostasis, yet our biochemical understanding of actinobacterial Clp enzymes derives almost entirely from mycobacteria, where their essentiality complicates efforts to understand their physiological behavior. Here, we reconstitute and biochemically characterize the ClpCP1P2 protease from Corynebacterium glutamicum, a genetically tractable actinobacterium in which clpC and clpX are non-essential. We find that, as in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, ClpP1 and ClpP2 are individually inactive and form an active peptidase only when stabilized by ATP-bound ClpC or acyldepsipeptide antibiotics, with further stimulation by N-blocked peptide agonists. However, C. glutamicum ClpCP1P2 exhibits faster kinetics and greater conformational stability than its mycobacterial orthologs, proteolyzing full-length substrates rapidly without requiring peptide agonists. We additionally show that the anti-mycobacterial antibiotics rufomycin and cyclomarin A bind the C. glutamicum ClpC N-terminal domain, exert substrate-specific effects on proteolysis, and impair C. glutamicum growth. The ability of these compounds to elicit toxicity through a non-essential target suggests that they act via gain-of-function dysregulation rather than simple inhibition. Together, our results validate C. glutamicum as a tractable model for interrogating Actinomycetota Clp proteases.

title: Secondary Solvation Shell Regulation for Fast-Charging Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: Most electrolyte strategies in lithium metal batteries (LMBs) target the first solvation shell or solvation diversity. However, such approaches have shown limited success in enabling fast-charging, as Li+ depletion inevitably develops at polarized interfaces. Here, we identify the secondary solvation shell as a critical regulator of fast-charging stability and show that a gradient solvation structure (GSS) overcomes ion depletion-induced failure.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Two-dimensional material membranes with precisely tunable interlayer spacing from nanometre to submillimetre
abstract: A deprotonation–ion coordination strategy is developed for microstructural engineering of layered material membranes, enabling the precise and reversible modulation of interlayer spacing over five orders of magnitude.

title: A Machine Learning Model Based on Ultrasound Radiomics and Multi-modal Clinical Features for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma in the Setting of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis
abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the value of multi-modal features (ultrasound characteristics, BRAF V600E mutation, and TPO-Ab) in predicting lymph node metastasis (LNM) of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) in the context of Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT), and to construct machine learning models for individualized risk assessment.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 377 patients with pathologically confirmed PTC and concurrent HT was enrolled and divided into LNM n=186 and non-LNM n=191 groups.

title: The key role of oxidation state and flake size in the ecotoxicological impact of industrial graphene oxide nanoflakes
abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) is a widely used nanomaterial across various scientific and technological fields. Environmental exposure to GO and consequent ecotoxicological effects have been largely reported. Despite the significant efforts and illuminating conclusions, establishing fair pairwise correlations between material and toxicity descriptors remains challenging and controversial. Key drawbacks in GO ecotoxicological studies to date include a lack of standardized materials, poorly defined descriptors, and insufficient material variants.

title: Distinct changes in brain and peripheral oxygen levels induced by synthetic opioids of the nitazene family
abstract: Nitazenes are a category of synthetic opioids, some of which have high analgesic potential but also high toxicity, which has historically prevented their development as therapeutic drugs. Like fentanyl, nitazenes induce respiratory depression, a primary factor in their toxicity. Recently, a nitazene derivative called N-desethyl-fluornitrazene (DFNZ) was shown to have high analgesic properties with weak hypoxic effects. To better characterize the hypoxic effects of DFNZ relative to its parent, fluornitrazene (FNZ) and the prototypical nitazene etonitazene, we used amperometric oxygen sensors in freely moving rats to examine oxygen dynamics in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and the subcutaneous space, using fentanyl as a comparison. All drugs induced similar patterns of subcutaneous hypoxia, with rapid dose-dependent oxygen decreases. In the NAc, all opioids, except DFNZ, at low iv doses (1-5 g/kg) induced moderate but significant brain oxygen increases. At higher doses (>10 g/kg), oxygen levels for all opioids, except DFNZ, showed a biphasic response; robust hypoxia followed by a weaker rebound-like hyperoxia. Etonitazene at 30 g/kg had the largest and most prolonged brain hypoxia compared to the other drugs, without the rebound-like hyperoxia. These findings indicate that etonitazene and FNZ mimic the effects of fentanyl, inducing dose-dependent brain and peripheral hypoxia. In contrast, DFNZ induces very weak hypoxia seen minimally at very high iv doses (300-1000 g/kg). Our findings substantiate the low hypoxic potency of DFNZ and indicate that not all nitazenes are characterized by high potential for toxicity. As such, the development of nitazenes as analgesics should not be categorically dismissed.

title: Trapping more seeing more, benchmarking a new trap column for low-input proteomics
abstract: Nanoflow liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (LC-MS) has become central to low-input and single-cell proteomics (SCP), where trap-and-elute workflows offer sample loading flexibility and analytical column protection but introduce additional dead volume, surface area, and a largely uncharacterized trade-off between flush direction and chromatographic performance. Here, we present a systematic, iterative benchmarking study of a purpose-built family of NanoShield trap columns against the established PepMap Neo trap cartridge and direct injection. Using a standardized workflow built on a commercial HeLa digest standard, we evaluated performance across two mass spectrometry platforms, multiple LC gradient lengths, both flush directions, and a range of sample input amounts and injection volumes. Shortening of the NanoShield packed bed, from an initial 5 cm format to a 1.2 cm format, closed a substantial sample loading time penalty and largely eliminated a pronounced forward-flush performance deficit, while remaining superior to the PepMap in reverse-flush mode and approaching direct injection level identification numbers, peak width, and quantitative precision. A next-generation NanoShield featuring a stationary phase with larger pore size further narrowed the residual forward-flush penalty. These results demonstrate that trap column bed length and stationary phase chemistry are key, partially independent design levers for closing the performance gap between trap-and-elute and direct injection workflows, and provide practical, present-day guidance for trap column selection and operation in low-input proteomics.

title: Computational identification and in vitro evaluation of astragaloside II as an inhibitor of dengue virus NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability
abstract: Background: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease in which severe cases are marked by leakage of plasma from blood vessels. The secreted nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) of dengue virus damages the endothelial barrier and is a drug target, but no approved antiviral exists. We aimed to identify compounds that target NS1 and to test whether the selected compound, astragaloside II (ASII), counteracts NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability.

title: Embodied schooling behavior via hydrodynamic interactions
abstract: Collective animal behavior is commonly explained by sensory-mediated interactions among individuals, yet physical interactions between moving bodies and their environment may also contribute to coordination. In fish schooling, passive hydrodynamic interactions have long been proposed to facilitate collective organization, but biological evidence remains limited because their effects are difficult to disentangle from active sensorimotor responses. Here, we combine computational simulations and physical experiments with self-propelled foils to identify balanced vortex interactions and develop a Vortex Balance Model (VBM) that predicts schooling configurations from swimming kinematics and relative tailbeat phase. We test these predictions using pairs of goldfish (Carassius auratus) swimming in a flow tank under three sensory conditions: intact vision and lateral-line sensing, visual deprivation with intact lateral-line sensing, and combined visual deprivation and reversible lateral-line impairment. Agreement between observed schooling configurations and VBM predictions increases as sensory input is reduced, reaching its highest level when both sensory modalities are impaired. These findings provide indirect biological evidence that passive hydrodynamic interactions contribute to fish schooling, while their effects can be modified or overridden by active sensorimotor responses.

title: Potential Energy Surfaces in Multilayered Form: Deep Learning Based Regression of Analytical Hierarchical Tree Structures Using Unstructured Clouds of Data-Points
abstract: In this work, we introduce analytical hierarchical tree structures, aka multilayered parametric functions, in the context of regression of multidimensional surfaces, such as molecular or interparticle potential energy surfaces. From a technical perspective, our binary trees stem from the ideas underlying the so-called hierarchical Tucker decomposition by replacing columnwise the factors by piecewise polynomials interpolated from randomized multivariate distributions. We refer to our approach as hierarchical Tucker finite basis representation (HT-FBR).
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Minimal, synthetic arginine deiminase pathway provides full ATP demand for cellular growth
abstract: Bottom-up construction of synthetic cells requires a simple, yet robust ATP-generating system. The arginine deiminase (ADI) pathway offers a minimal, enzyme-based alternative to more complex ATP-producing systems such as glycolytic routes, respiratory chains or photosystems. Here, we implement the ADI pathway in Escherichia coli and test its capacity to fully replace native ATP generation. First, we designed and tested synthetic ADI operons through combinatorial library screening and selected high-performing variants. Using the best performing-ADI variant, we progressively reduced the cells dependence on native ATP generation while increasing selection for ADI-dependent growth through targeted knockout strains and growth conditions, followed by adaptive laboratory evolution. This resulted in a strain in which the ADI pathway sustained growth in minimal medium at a doubling time of 21 hours, serving as the sole source of ATP. Whole-genome sequencing of evolved strains revealed that this transition required loss-of-function mutations in the native respiratory chain. These findings demonstrate that the ATP supply of a cell can be fully supported by the ADI pathway, which has not been demonstrated in nature. Moreover, the ability of the pathway to sustain growth with a relatively high growth rate highlights its potential to fully power synthetic cells and support other biotechnological applications.

title: Predictive Modeling in Mining Production: A Systematic Review of Methodological Trends, Analytical Maturity, and Smart Mining Systems
abstract: Background: The growing digitalization of the mining sector has accelerated the adoption of predictive analytics to improve operational efficiency and reduce uncertainty in mineral production systems. In this context, predictive modeling has established itself as a strategic tool for addressing the dynamic complexity and geological heterogeneity of mining operations. This study presents a systematic review aimed at identifying, analyzing, and classifying the methodological approaches used in predictive models applied to mineral production.

title: Nose-to-Brain Delivery of Cocaine in Mice: A Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model Incorporating Olfactory Epithelial Transport, Mucociliary Clearance, and Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability
abstract: Intranasal (IN) cocaine produces rapid central nervous system (CNS) effects despite generating substantially lower plasma concentrations than equivalent intravenous (IV) doses, suggesting a direct nose-to-brain pathway. The olfactory epithelium provides anatomical continuity for cocaine to pass between the nasal cavity and the brain. Quantifying the relative contribution of this pathway to total brain cocaine exposure requires a physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that explicitly accounts for nasal mucosal architecture, epithelial transport barriers, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability. Here we used tandem mass spectrometry to collect cocaine concentration-time data from the brain and plasma of awake mice administered IV or IN cocaine and leveraged that data to generate such a framework. Our results provide evidence that following IN cocaine, the olfactory pathway accounts for approximately half of the cocaine that reaches the brain. The mechanistic PBPK framework developed here, incorporating anatomically grounded nasal compartment separation, blood-flow-scaled mucosal absorption, tissue diffusion resistance, mucociliary clearance, plasma protein binding, and BBB permeability-surface area transport, substantially improves upon empirical one-compartment absorption models and produces parameter estimates with physiological interpretability. The proportionate efficiency of the olfactory route relative to systemic absorption may provide a pharmacokinetic basis for the rapid onset of IN cocaines CNS effects and has direct implications for understanding the psychoactive effects of cocaine.

title: Genome-Guided Discovery and Biosynthetic Characterization of Burkstatins, Bicyclic Microviridins with Protease Inhibitory Activity
abstract: Microviridins are ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides characterized by a highly constrained macrocyclic scaffold and potent serine protease inhibitory activity. Unlike canonical tricyclic microviridins, bicyclic microviridins, exemplified by marinostatins, lack the characteristic {omega}-amide linkage. The biosynthetic diversity and biological activities of bicyclic microviridins remain poorly explored. Here, genome mining and phylogenetic analyses revealed diverse lineages of putative bicyclic microviridins, including a conserved family of multicore precursors in Burkholderiaceae. We characterized a representative biosynthetic gene cluster from Paraburkholderia sp. CNPSo 3076 and demonstrated that a single ATP-grasp ligase, BksD, catalyzes the formation of two {omega}-ester macrocycles within each of the two precursor core regions. Heterologous reconstitution and tandem mass spectrometric analyses enabled the production and structural characterization of two bicyclic peptides, designated burkstatin 1 and burkstatin 2. Despite sharing a conserved bicyclic scaffold, the two peptides exhibited distinct serine protease inhibitory profiles. Burkstatin 2 potently inhibited subtilisin and elastase, whereas burkstatin 1 displayed weaker subtilisin inhibition and no detectable elastase inhibition. These findings expand the known biosynthetic and functional diversity of bicyclic microviridins, demonstrate the capacity of a single ATP-grasp ligase to modify multiple core peptides and highlight the influence of core sequence variation on protease inhibitory activity.

title: The activation-deactivation cycle of human PIEZO1
abstract: PIEZO1 is a cation channel that is primarily activated through mechanical force, and activation has been shown to be influenced by membrane curvature. PIEZO1 is ubiquitously expressed and plays critical roles in various patho-/physiological processes such as inflammatory diseases or red blood cell volume regulation. Here we combine coarse-grained and atomistic simulations in which human PIEZO1 is embedded in a curved membrane and subjected to simulations under controlled membrane tension and a physiological transmembrane potential, allowing the gating cycle to be reconstructed at atomic resolution. Systematic pressure adaptation identifies an activation regime in which the channel flattens progressively, and ion permeation quantitatively reproduces the experimental conductance of 36 pS. Furthermore, the R2456-E2117 salt bridge couples pore lipid retention to the anchor domain and disrupting it reproduces the phenotypes of the disease-associated R2456H and R2456C variants. PIEZO activation is transmitted through an interconnected network of contact rearrangements that ultimately reshapes the yoda1 binding pocket at the THU8/THU9 interface. This state-dependent remodelling rationalises the pharmacology of yoda1 and offers a framework for the structure-based design of PIEZO1 modulators.

title: Structural Context Collapse in Deep-Learning Predictors: A Benchmark of Outer Membrane Protein Loop Decontextualization and a Backbone-Centric Filter for Surface Epitope Identification
abstract: Deep-learning structure predictors (AlphaFold2, ESMFold) require global context. Modeling outer membrane protein (OMP) loops without transmembrane scaffolds creates an out-of-distribution challenge. Across 28 non-redundant OMP crystal structures (1.40–3.10 Å), isolated loops collapsed, inverting core solvent accessibility (native core RSA: 3.6 ± 0.7% inverted to 58.7 ± 4.5% [AF2] and 62.1 ± 4.8% [ESMFold] for buried positions; mean loop RSA: 32.1 ± 10.0%), yielding 0.00% true negative rate (0/28 retaining core burial; 95% Clopper–Pearson CI: [0.00%, 10.15%]) across RSA thresholds 5%–20%.

title: A Highly Active and Promiscuous Esterase for Amide Bond Synthesis under Aqueous Conditions
abstract: A growing number of hydrolase enzymes show acyltransferase activity under aqueous conditions. However, the competing hydrolysis reaction and the limited catalytic rates for these enzymes prevent them from being routinely used for synthetic applications. To find improved enzymes, we generated an enzyme panel based on promiscuous acyltransferase template enzymes. We identified SoEst12, a highly active and selective enzyme belonging to the family VIII carboxylesterases. Kinetics show that this enzyme is up to 8600× faster (kcatapp) than the well-studied PestE using a model reaction for amidation and that its impressive activity is not limited to the model ester. Enzyme loading studies coupled with the kinetics showed a kinetically controlled selectivity for amidation over hydrolysis, which can be best exploited when using a low enzyme loading. SoEst12 displays a wide amine substrate scope with no hydrolysis of the amide product formed. Competing hydrolysis with some of the ester substrates has been reduced by the introduction of a point mutation in the family-conserved WGG motif. Modeling of these point mutants showed that the reduced hydrolysis activity is correlated with an improved affinity for the amine. The SoEst12 crystal structure was solved, and the N-terminus of a cleaved tag of a symmetry neighbor was found inserted into the active site of the enzyme close to a bound acetate, suggesting a “cleaved amide” and giving mechanistic insight into the high activity and selectivity shown by SoEst12. We demonstrate the synthetic potential of SoEst12 by synthesizing the antiarrhythmic drug procainamide and an AKT inhibitor intermediate in buffer using a low biocatalyst loading.

title: Unsupervised reward-driven image segmentation in automated scanning transmission electron microscopy experiments.
abstract: Automated experiments in scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) require rapid image segmentation to optimize the data representation for human interpretation, decision-making, site-selective spectroscopy, and atomic manipulation. Currently, segmentation tasks are typically performed using supervised machine learning methods, which require human-labeled data and are sensitive to out-of-distribution drift effects caused by changes in resolution, sampling, or beam shape.

title: De Novo Design of C-H Hydroxylation Enzymes with Programmed Selectivities
abstract: The ability to precisely functionalize individual C-H bonds in complex organic molecules would transform synthetic strategies to produce essential chemicals. In nature, C-H oxidations are commonly achieved using metalloenzymes such as cytochrome P450s, however adapting these systems to achieve selective conversions of complex substrates requires extensive enzyme discovery and engineering campaigns. Here we show that selective C-H oxidation biocatalysts can be programmed computationally from minimal structural inputs comprising a Cys-ligated heme cofactor, catalytic side chains required for H2O2 activation and heterolysis, and the target substrate precisely positioned adjacent to the resulting ferryl intermediate (Compound I). We designed heme hydroxylases for increasingly complex substrates, progressing from aromatic and aliphatic oxidations of fluorogenic model compounds to regiodivergent oxidation of estradiol at either the benzylic C6 (93% d.e.) or unactivated C16 (99% d.e.) positions. Crystal structures across all campaigns confirm the accuracy of the design pipeline. Together, these results establish a general framework for constructing selective heme hydroxylases around predefined substrates and reaction geometries, providing a path toward custom biocatalysts for site-selective C-H functionalizations.

title: Comment: Transforming chemical education through industry collaboration
authors: Ashley Mahoney, chair, Committee on Professional Training

title: Classical structural priors improve neural molecular representations in molecule language models
abstract: Classical molecular similarity is central to chemical information systems, yet molecule-language models trained on paired structure-text data do not necessarily organize molecular embeddings according to graded structural relationships. Here we introduce Structure-Aware Guided Alignment (SAGA), a training-only regularizer that uses Centered Kernel Alignment to align neural molecular representations with fingerprint-based Tanimoto similarity, without adding parameters or requiring fingerprints at inference. In MolCA and Atomas, SAGA improves molecule-text retrieval, shifts non-exact retrieval toward closer structural analogues, and increases average scaffold-split property-prediction performance, while molecular description and text-to-molecule generation are improved or preserved in single-run ablations. These results show that established chemoinformatics priors can make molecule-language representations more chemically faithful while retaining their multimodal utility.

title: Multiple moiré polarization textures in twisted trilayers
abstract: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moiré-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in some twisted trilayers, where the relative moiré phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI$_3$ and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, it is clarified how the relative moiré phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture by layer sliding. The multiple moiré polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moiré patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.

title: Integrative Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Identify ARG1 and S100A12 as Novel Biomarkers Associated with Innate Immune Barrier Dysfunction in Psoriasis
abstract: Background: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease in which the dysfunction of the innate immune cell barrier (IICB) is implicated. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. This study aimed to identify and characterize IICB-related biomarkers and their regulatory networks, thereby elucidating their roles in psoriasis pathogenesis. Methods: We obtained psoriasis-related transcriptomic datasets and a list of IICB-related genes (IICB-RGs) from public databases and the literature.

title: ProtFlap: Structure-based Deep Learning Prediction of Protein Flexibility from Atomic Energy Networks
abstract: Protein flexibility is a key determinant of molecular recognition, catalysis, and regulation, yet remains difficult to characterise at scale. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed descriptions of time-dependent dynamics but are computationally expensive.
