Although recent AI-based structure prediction methods have substantially improved access to high-quality static protein structures, they inherently lack information regarding the dynamic fluctuations essential for functional understanding.

title: Nanodisc-Enabled Dissection of GxxxG- Mediated Amyloid Beta Oligomerization Mechanisms
abstract: Extracellular deposition of amyloid plaques is a major hallmark in Alzheimers disease, in which amyloid-beta fibrils are key constituents. Fibrillation of amyloid-beta is modulated by several key sequence motifs, among which the G33LMVG37 motif located in the C-terminal is particularly significant. Moreover, the interaction between amyloid-beta and cellular membrane can be determining factor in its oligomerization.

title: AI and experiments reveal impurities hindering waste plastic pyrolysis oil recycling
abstract: A Korean research team has identified how impurities interfere with the use of waste plastic pyrolysis oil as a petrochemical feedstock through catalytic experiments and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational chemistry. The findings, published in the journal ACS Catalysis, provide a scientific basis for predicting potential declines in catalytic performance according to the types and concentrations of impurities present.

title: Disrupting Hidden Antiaromaticity in N -Hydroxyphthalimide Reveals a Design Principle for Highly Reactive N -Oxyl Hydrogen Atom Transfer Mediators
abstract: N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) and its corresponding N-oxyl radical, phthalimide N-oxyl (PINO), have long been used as mediators for hydrogen atom transfer (HAT), particularly in radical-mediated C–H oxidations. Although numerous NHPI/PINO derivatives have been developed, the absence of an intuitive model connecting scaffold structure to intrinsic HAT reactivity has left catalyst development largely empirical.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Neuroprotective Effects of the Purine-Derived Compound ITH15004 Against Nigericin- and Mitochondria-Induced Toxicity in NSC-34 Motor Neuron-like Cells
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the progressive degeneration of motor neurons. Most patients die within 3 to 5 years of diagnosis, primarily due to respiratory failure, and effective therapeutic options remain limited. Mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, calcium dysregulation, and neuroinflammation are key contributors to ALS pathogenesis.
authors: P. K. de Moraes Berenguel Lossavaro

title: Deep sequence-function mapping reveals computationally unpredictable epistatic trajectories that drive laboratory evolution
abstract: The black-box nature of directed evolution has been constraining advances in enzyme engineering and the wider application of engineered biocatalysts. While conventional deep sequence-function mapping has delivered insights into sequence space architecture, it lacks the ability to analyse adaptive landscapes and fully grasp the long-term impact of epistasis on the accessibility of evolutionary trajectories. Here, we introduce Deep Evolutionary Trajectory Mapping (dETM) which tracks the winners of a multi-round evolutionary campaign to map catalytic rates across the adaptive landscape of an imine reductase. We identified founder variants as stepping stones towards fitness peaks and recognise positive epistasis as their competitive advantage over alternative lineages. State-of-the-art machine learning models could not predict the resulting winning trajectories, which highlights the importance of decoding design principles for successful evolution experimentally. Permissive selection and ultrahigh-throughput screening emerge as foundations of derisking landscape traversal by keeping multiple paths accessible and avoiding diminishing returns.

title: Structural basis of SBDS dysfunction in Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome
abstract: Surveillance of functional centers in the mature 60S ribosomal subunit by SBDS licenses its translational debut. Timely release of eIF6 from 60S by SBDS is essential to permit 40S joining. Biallelic mutations in SBDS associated with Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS), an inherited ribosomopathy, impair dissociation of eIF6 from 60S. How SBDS variants that bind to 60S structurally perturb the maturation and surveillance of 60S is yet to be deciphered.

title: From Self-Driving Laboratories to Connected Experimentation in the Physical Sciences: Lessons from the Critical Materials Value Chain
abstract: Self-driving laboratories close the loop between prediction, synthesis, and measurement on individual platforms, yet most physical-science research outside user facilities proceeds through multistage workflows distributed across separate laboratories, with manual handoffs of samples, protocols, and data. This review assesses how autonomous experimentation can extend across such workflows, using the critical minerals and materials value chain for energy technologies as a use case.

title: Coupling Metallaarsinidene and Methylene Groups to an Arsavinyl [As=CH 2 ] – Ligand; a Softer Pnictovinyl Is a Harder Molecular Switch
Transparent Multitask Surface Enhanced Raman Spectral Analysis of Catecholamines with Explainable AI
abstract: Surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides a highly sensitive detection of biomolecules; however, interpretation of these high dimensional data is challenging and requires the use of advanced spectra analytical techniques such as machine learning models. These models lack transparency and interpretability, limiting their acceptance in real-world applications. Understanding the rationale behind machine learning predictions would enhance transparency and build confidence among chemical and biomedical researchers.

title: On the Molecular Structure of Coordination-Driven Self-Assembled Cofacial Porphyrin Prisms
abstract: Dinuclear metalloarene complexes bridged by a 2,5-dihydroxy-1,4-benzoquinato (dhbq) ligand are a class of “molecular clip” used to tether two meso-tetra(4-pyridyl)porphyrins in a cofacial arrangement. Despite their common use, there is a conspicuous lack of crystallographic or other structural characterization on these diporphyrin assemblies. Here we report the synthesis and characterization of six cofacial prisms strategically chosen to probe molecular structure. Moreover, we present the first two crystal structures of dhbq-clipped cofacial porphyrin prisms.

title: LLaMalysis: Language-guided inverse design of catalyst surfaces with targeted hydrogen adsorption energies
abstract: Computational catalyst discovery is constrained by vast compositional and structural spaces, whereas atomistic generative models typically rely on engineered conditioning variables. Here we formulate catalyst inverse design as an instruction-following task in which compositional and catalytic requirements are expressed in natural language. We fine-tune an instruction-tuned language model on serialized catalyst slabs from the Open Catalyst 2020 dataset and obtain a generator with validity and uniqueness comparable to catalyst-specific baselines.

title: Adhesion decides whether a membrane buds; leaflet asymmetry decides which way
abstract: A cell exposed to nanoparticles takes them in and sheds vesicles outward using the same membrane. We ask what decides the direction. The energy of a completed spherical bud is a quadratic in its radius, and an adhering particle enters only the quadratic coefficient while a leaflet area asymmetry enters only the linear one. Adhesion is therefore isotropic: it decides whether a bud forms and cannot select a direction. Leaflet asymmetry is directional: its sign selects one. Endocytosis and ectosome shedding become one mechanism separated by a change of sign.

title: para-Selective Dearomatization of N-Arylhydroxylamines for Modular Quinone Imine Synthesis
abstract: Dearomatization of arenes represents a pivotal transformation in organic synthesis, enabling direct access to alicyclic scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules. Quinone imines, though highly valuable as synthetic intermediates for complex natural products, remain challenging to prepare and isolate. We herein report a metal- and oxidant-free strategy for the modular synthesis of quinone imines through fluorosulfuryl imidazolium triflate-mediated para-selective dearomatization of N-arylhydroxylamines under mild conditions.

title: Consequential Life Cycle Assessment Impacts of U.S. Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Exports
abstract: What is the net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions impact of U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports? Conclusions in the peer-reviewed literature range from a net reduction through global fuel switching from coal to natural gas, to net increase through entrenched fossil fuel dependencies and delayed deployment of low-carbon technologies. In this work, we combine an integrated assessment model with a measurement informed GHG intensity model of global LNG supply chains to assess the impact of eliminating US LNG exports on global GHG emissions from 2020 through 2050.

title: Pericón ( Tagetes lucida ) extract in gelatin films: a colorimetric ammonia indicator for smart packaging
Chemistry Lab Notebook for Obsidian: An ELN for CDX and CDXML Reaction Files
abstract: We describe the Chemistry Lab Notebook for Obsidian, an electronic laboratory notebook (ELN) for synthetic chemistry. Each Markdown reaction note is linked to a CDX or CDXML file drawn in ChemDraw or in the free Reactio Draw. The notebook's plugins display the reaction scheme and reagent table of this file in the note and search all reactions by structure, role or whole reaction. They also draft characterization paragraphs from the note fields and export Open Reaction Database records and PubChem deposition files.

title: Feeding A Thia-Prins Baby: A Pseudo-Telescopic Approach to Functionalized Tetrahydrothiopyranes
abstract: More than seven decades after its discovery, the thia-Prins reaction remains underdeveloped as a preparative route to saturated sulfur heterocycles. Its expansion offers access to tetrahydrothiopyrans in which carbonyl-derived substitution, C4 functionality, and sulfur oxidation state can be varied within a common synthetic approach. Here, we demonstrate that downstream functionalization can overcome the product-isolation problem that has restricted the reaction’s preparative use.

title: Autonomous phase diagram mapping of polymer blends through SAXS-guided active learning
abstract: Autonomous phase behavior mapping from multicomponent copolymer formulation requires feedback that connects scattering measurements to experimental decisions. We couple robotic polymer formulation, automated small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analysis, and Gaussian-process active learning using structure factor to autonomously map complex phase behavior of multiblock copolymer/homopolymer blends.

title: Chemistry of Materials Highlights the Future of Light-Emitting Materials
A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
abstract: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. Equilibrium temperatures are given for both a theoretical lumped body and for a slab body, in which thermal conduction is considered. All data are limited to the solid state, up to a material-specific upper temperature limit. Currently, the database applies to extraterrestrial (AM0) sunlight only. A graphical App is also provided for exploring and visualizing the database.

title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

title: Computational Drug Discovery of Natural Product Compounds for Tyrosinase Inhibition
abstract: Plants produce chemically diverse compounds for defence and survival, many of which exhibit biological activity and offer promising starting points for drug discovery. This study thus investigated natural compounds as potential inhibitors of tyrosinase, a key enzyme in melanin production and an established target in the treatment of hyperpigmentation. A quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) machine-learning model was developed using ChEMBL tyrosinase bioactivity data and property-matched decoys.

title: Bipolar Faradaic Water Dissociation in Bipolar Membranes
abstract: Water dissociation (WD, H2O → H+ + OH−) in bipolar membrane (BPM) junctions enables pH-asymmetric electrochemical devices, but the microscopic role of conductive WD catalysts remains unresolved. Here we show that conductive catalyst layers can drive nominally non-faradaic water dissociation through two spatially separated bipolar faradaic reactions. In this mechanism, the alkaline-side interface of the WD catalyst layer is polarized cathodically and reduces water by interfacial proton-coupled electron transfer (I-PCET) to form adsorbed or absorbed H equivalents and OH−, whereas the…

title: Dual-Modality Attomolar Detection of DNA Hybridization Using Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity
abstract: Spin-selective charge transfer through DNA has emerged as a promising approach for DNA hybridization detection. However, the minimum DNA concentration at which a reliable spin-dependent signal can be experimentally observed remains unclear. Here, by employing the CISS effect, we report a dual-modality electrical and optical approach for detecting DNA hybridization. In electrical detection, we used a customized two-probe printed circuit board, which transduces a molecular-scale spin-based signal into a measurable macroscopic electrical signal.

title: Matched Metal–Organic Frameworks Reveal How Chemistry and Pore Structure Shape Gas Adsorption
abstract: Designing metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for adsorption requires distinguishing pore-chemistry associations from differences in architecture. An outcome-independent matched-comparison analysis of the ARC–MOF v7 simulation database pairs frameworks with identical topology and dimensionality and closely constrained values of seven pore descriptors. The resulting 13,072 chemistry-changing pairs are benchmarked against similarly matched pairs with unchanged represented chemistry labels.

title: Assessing the transfer-learning performance of foundation models for energetic materials property prediction under low-data conditions
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of off-the-shelf foundation model embeddings provided by CheMeleon, MolCLR, and MACE-OFF to predict energetic material properties from sparse datasets. Models were trained to predict crystal density, heat of formation and impact sensitivity from SMILES strings, with performance benchmarked against molecular representations provided by Morgan fingerprints and hand-crafted descriptors.

title: A Novel Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7// Li4Ti5O12 Dual-Ion High Power Battery
abstract: Concerns over lithium abundance and safety have driven the search for alternatives to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising owing to sodium’s abundance and low cost, but sluggish Na+ diffusion and limited rate capability hinder their practical use in high power batteries. Here we report a mixed (Li/Na)-ion battery as a low-cost, high-power alternative solution. We demonstrate a novel mixed-ion Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7(NFPP)//Li4Ti5O12(LTO) full cell operating in a lithium-based electrolyte with excellent performance.

title: Effect of PDMS Sponge-Derived Silicon Oxycarbide Particles on Water Incorporation and Rheology in PDMS–THF Mixtures
abstract: Here we report preparing silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) particles from the commercially available polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), with radically different morphologies depending on the processing conditions. We first prepare PDMS sponge, which acts as the precursor material for the SiOC particles, by heating a solution of PDMS and cross-linker in THF with suitable concentrations. The cross-linking reaction simultaneously occurring with the bubble formation from boiling the THF results in the formation of a sponge.

title: Artemisitene converts cysteine to dehydroalanine via a cascade reaction involving: (i) thiol-Michael reaction, (ii) oxidation of the sulfur atom, and (iii) elimination
abstract: Artemisitene, which contains both an activated olefin and an endoperoxide, is a plant natural product isolated from the medicinal plant, Artemisia annua. Recent efforts in our research laboratory have shown that a related sesquiterpenoid, arteannuin B, undergoes a thiol-Michael addition with cysteine. Therefore, we hypothesized that the presence of the α,β-unsaturated lactone in artemisitene, would also result in a nucleophilic addition of the thiol moiety of cysteine, and this adduct would also result in an oxidation to yield dehydroalanine.

title: Mesoporous Separator Engineering Rectified Electrolyte Chemistry for Durable Non-Aqueous Aluminium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Rechargeable non-aqueous aluminium-ion batteries (AIBs) are promising low-cost and sustainable energy storage systems, but their development is hindered by sluggish transport of strongly associated chloroaluminate ions and unstable aluminium plating/stripping. Here we demonstrate that engineering the separator microenvironment effectively regulates electrolyte chemistry and interfacial ion transport in AIBs. A binder-free dendritic mesoporous silicamodified glass fiber (DMS-GF) separator is developed by growing DMS nanoparticles directly 2 at the GF scaffold surface.

title: Orbital-Optimized Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory Within the Tamm-Dancoff Approximation Using Lagrangian Minimization
abstract: Time-dependent density functional theory in the Tamm-Dancoff approximation (TDDFT/TDA) is a computationally tractable approach for calculating excited electronic state energies and properties. TDDFT/TDA constructs single-excitation electronic states from Kohn-Sham molecular orbitals where the occupied orbitals have been variationally optimized according to the Aufbau principle and the virtual orbitals are left unrelaxed.

title: History-Dependent and Irreversible Restructuring of Molecular Cu–N–C Catalysts
abstract: Copper–nitrogen–carbon (Cu–N–C) catalysts have been widely investigated for cathodic electrocatalysis, yet identifying Cu species under operating conditions and establishing structural reversibility remain challenging due to their dynamic restructuring. Here, we investigate the potential- and history-dependent evolution of a structurally well-defined Cu porphyrin model catalyst using cyclic voltammetry-coupled in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy (CV-XAS), complemented by high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected XAS, Raman spectroscopy, and identical-location electron microscopy.

title: A vacated second ligand site acts as a decoy in redocking: systematic in P-glycoprotein, intermittent across eight other proteins
abstract: Redocking tests whether a docking protocol can recover a deposited pose: the ligand is removed and the program is asked to put it back. Standard preparation deletes every copy. When a structure contains two copies in one cavity, the receptor passed to the program was never observed empty. We measured the effect of that deletion in deposited human P-glycoprotein structures, with the search box centred on the deposited pose so that a failure cannot be blamed on site finding. Across 15 structures the median top-pose RMSD is 8.30 Å and 1 of 15 falls within 2.0 Å.

title: Reticular Programming of Gold Nanocluster Electronic States Enables Near-Unity Faradaic Efficiency in Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Achieving selective nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis requires more than accelerating nitrate activation: the catalyst must sustain eight-electron reduction while preventing premature intermediate release and competing hydrogen evolution. Yet controlling these competing processes through the molecular architecture surrounding well-defined metal centers remains challenging.

title: From Divergence to Coupling: Interfacial Water and Adsorbed Hydrogen during Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: The structure of interfacial water is widely invoked to explain the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet how it evolves relative to adsorbed hydrogen (H*) and responds to changes in electrode potential remains unclear. Here, we simultaneously track interfacial water and H* on platinum during potential pulses using Dynamic Response Spectroscopy (DRS), which separates interfacial-and diffusion-layer contributions to the measured spectra.

title: Multilevel Reproducibility Assessment of Polymer Monolithic Capillary Columns for Peptide Separations
abstract: Polymer monoliths have emerged as attractive stationary phases for peptide and intact-protein analysis, offering an alternative to packed-bed columns. Their synthesis involves several critical manual steps raising concerns about reproducibility and transferability of the synthesis protocol. This study systematically evaluates the robustness and reproducibility of an established synthesis protocol where two operators synthesized two of column batches of 100 µm i.d. poly(styrene-co-divinylbenzene) monolithic capillary columns and assessing their performance in peptide separations.

title: Short-circuit-resistant sulfide solid-state batteries through lithium dewetting
abstract: In sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries, lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte indiscriminately through grain boundaries, interparticle voids and pores, causing internal short circuits that accelerate degradation and terminate cell life. This penetration has been understood largely in mechanical terms, and mitigation has focused on suppressing cracks. Here we show that chemical wetting, governed by the lithium/electrolyte interfacial energy, is a decisive factor in lithium penetration.

title: Computational Studies on the Stability of BINOL-CPA/Imine Complexes
abstract: Chiral BINOL-derived phosphoric acids (CPAs) are widely used Brønsted acid catalysts in enantioselective synthesis, where the relative stabilities of experimentally accessible binary CPA/imine complexes have been linked to stereoselectivity, yet previous quantum-chemical studies using implicit solvation showed substantial deviations from their observed E/Z ratios.

title: Photoinduced Direct N-Arylation of Nitroalkanes at Ambient Temperature via 1,2-Boronate Shift
abstract: Although photoexcited nitroarenes have been explored for facile reductive couplings, owing to their higher energetic n→π* electronic transition compared to the nitroarenes, the metal-free reductive C-N coupling reaction with nitroalkane under the photochemical condition is not known. We report, for the first time, the photoexcitation of nitroalkanes and their participation in metal- and photocatalyst-free reductive C−N coupling with arylboronic acids at ambient temperature via 1,2-boronate shift.

title: An environment-conditioned QM/MM resource for protein–ligand electron densities and quantum-informed pose rescoring
abstract: Structure-based drug design relies on geometric and empirical features, whereas electron density encodes polarization and weak interactions but is costly to obtain at biomolecular scale. We present a multilevel QM/MM resource from MISATO trajectories and PDBbind complexes, comprising 104,636 electronic-structure records across 96,467 geometries. Physics-embedded equivariant surrogates achieve 0.326–0.384% density NMAE on PDB-disjoint tests with explicit TIP3P water; predicted receptor electrostatic potentials agree with reference values (Pearson r = 0.99529).

title: Pre-Nucleation Conformational Ordering Revealed by Optical Trapping Raman Microspectroscopy
abstract: During molecular crystal nucleation, solute molecules are forced to adopt positions, orientations, and conformations consistent with the crystal lattice. Although positional and orientational ordering during crystal nucleation have been extensively investigated, the evolution of conformational order remains poorly understood, despite its importance in determining crystal polymorphism. In this study, we monitored the evolution of conformational order during crystal nucleation using in situ Raman microspectroscopy combined with optical trapping.

title: Plasma-Enhanced Surface Doping SnNiOx Nanofilms for Water Oxidation
abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) limits the efficiency of alkaline water electrolysis, and the rational design of non-precious-metal anodes requires an understanding of how a dopant modifies an oxide surface. Although atomically dispersed catalysts (ADCs) offer high intrinsic activity, precise synthesis and characterization of their local active sites remain challenging. Surface doping provides a tractable alternative for probing intrinsic activity and correlating it with the dopant coordination environment.

title: Resin 3D Printing with Dose-Controlled Solubility
abstract: Vat photopolymerization (VP) offers high resolution and throughput with low surface roughness, but requires support structures that limit printable geometries, generate non-recyclable waste, and must be removed manually. We introduce dose-controlled selective solubility vat photopolymerization (dSSVP), wherein a low 405 nm light dose forms linear acrylate chains, while high doses deplete a base quencher and initiate cationic epoxide polymerization to form a solvent-resistant crosslinked network.

title: Ligand Topology, Homoconjugation and Flexibility in Pyridine-Pyrrolide Tetrel(IV) Complexes Dictate Excited State Decay
Intrinsic Excitation Polarization across the Exciton Manifold of Individual Molecular Nanotubes
abstract: The polarization of excitonic transitions provides insight into molecular organization, but ensemble spectroscopy averages over many assemblies, while photoluminescence measurements at the level of individual assemblies predominantly probe their lowest-energy excitonic states. Here, we use polarizationresolved photoluminescence-excitation microscopy to probe higher-energy excitonic states in individual double-walled molecular nanotubes (DWNTs).

title: Deconvolution for high-resolution oversampling MALDI MSI
abstract: Decreasing pixel size is essential to resolve single cells via mass spectrometry imaging. Here, we present a bioanalytical and computational pipeline to perform oversampling MALDI-MSI from tissues and cells and deconvolve oversampled MALDI-MSI results. By comparing to histochemical staining and fluorescence microscopy, we can show that deconvolution improves the quality of resulting images compared to unprocessed MALDI-MSI data. Despite the signal loss due to oversampling compared to regular MALDI-MSI data acquisition, we can obtain 166 annotations in positive-ion mode for mouse kidney.

title: Novel Triple-action Pt(IV) prodrugs with carbocyanine and chalcone in axial position: photoactivation, tumor targeting, fluorescent tumor visualization, and high therapeutic efficacy
abstract: Pt(IV) prodrugs are highly promising platform for anticancer agents due to the ability to fine-tune the structure and properties of the prodrug by varying the axial ligand conjugated with the Pt(IV) core. In this study, we have synthesized photoactivated Pt(IV) prodrugs with NIR-absorbing cyanine and chalcone in axial positions, which combine the advantages of dual-target chemotherapy, controlled photoactivation, photodynamic therapy, and fluorescent NIR bioimaging.

title: What we know and what we don’t: an audit of experimental solid-electrolyte data, and the patent literature as an untapped source
abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are trained on experimental ionic-conductivity data, yet public datasets are smaller, more duplicated and noisier than their sizes suggest. We merged the five open Li conductivity datasets we could download (Liverpool Ionics, Laskowski et al., McHaffie et al., OBELiX and the text-mined set of Shon and Min) and audited them in three ways.

title: Action-Conditioned Sparse Mixture-of-Experts World Model for Predicting Microplate Observations in Robotic Chemistry
abstract: Automated chemistry requires both reaction-outcome prediction and monitoring of the physical execution of experiments. We study an action-conditioned model for predicting welllevel plate observations after robotic operations. The architecture combines address-masked action injection, sparse experts routed by a chemistry-oriented scene descriptor, and a gated pyramid decoder for local refinement. In the reported trajectory evaluation, the model reaches PSNR 29.6 and failure-detection F1 0.79 at 7.6 GFLOPs and 118 ms per plate.

title: A coupled experimental-modeling framework for evaluating the electrochemical performance of lithium-ion battery electrodes remanufactured with recycled LiFePO 4
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicle and electronics markets is generating a rising volume of endof-life batteries, making recycling essential to recover critical materials and reduce environmental impact. The electrochemical performance of future recycled batteries needs to be optimized by identifying the best remanufacturing parameters. Here, we propose a coupled experimental and computational framework that moves towards this objective by using the recycling of LiFePO 4 (LFP) as a proof-of-concept.

title: The ADAPT Map: circuit rewrites and over-conjugated states in ADAPT-VQE
abstract: Variational quantum circuits are usually judged by the energy they reach. We ask by what route ADAPTVQE reaches the ground state, and follow both the optimized angles of all its circuits, tabulated as the ADAPT Map, and the bond orders of the state optimized at each depth. In three polyenes, an H6 chain, and benzene, re-optimization hardly changes the earlier angles up to a system-dependent depth. At that depth the change jumps by an order of magnitude and a generator already in the circuit is selected again with the opposite sign, while the convergence curve shows at most a change of pace.

title: Novelty-stratified external validation of free in silico ADMET tools
abstract: Background and Purpose. Freely available in silico ADMET platforms are used routinely to triage compounds, yet each is validated by its own developers on its own training data, so reported accuracies are neither comparable across tools nor tested on novel chemistry. We asked whether any platform is generally superior, and whether structural novelty affects all endpoints alike. Experimental Approach.

title: Uranium Hydride Complexes for Dinitrogen Activation
Predicting rectilinear chain packing
abstract: Predicting rectilinear polymer crystal structures remains challenging because chain connectivity and three-dimensional crystal packing must be determined simultaneously. Conventional molecular-crystal CSP approaches assume discrete molecular building blocks and are therefore not directly applicable to the coupled problem of polymer topology and crystal organization.

title: Oxidized monoglycosylceramides modulate lipid antigenmediated immune responses through higher-affinity binding to CD1d
abstract: Glycolipids are key mediators of immune regulation, yet their biological functions may be altered by oxidative modifications. The brain and nervous system are particularly prone to such modifications due to the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and the abundance of glycolipids containing unsaturated fatty acids. Both oxidative stress and the accumulation of glucosylceramide (GlcCer) have been implicated in neurological disorders. However, the immunological properties of oxidized glycolipids remain largely unexplored.

title: Solving Molecular Crystal Structures through Experimental PXRD-Guided Sequential Crystal Structure Prediction
abstract: Structure determination of organic molecular crystals relies heavily on single-crystal X-ray diffraction, yet suitable single crystals are often difficult to obtain. A common alternative uses crystal structure prediction (CSP) to generate candidate structures for subsequent comparison with experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns. Such trial-and-error searches across multiple space groups incur substantial computational costs. Here, we introduce a structure determination protocol that uses experimental PXRD together with molecular structure as inputs to guide CSP from the outset.

title: Benchmarking the Predictive Performance and Computational Cost of Machine Learning Models for Functional Group Identification from Experimental Infrared Spectra
abstract: Automated functional group identification from infrared (IR) spectra has attracted a wide range of machine learning architectures, but differences in datasets, training protocols, and reported metrics hinder direct comparison. Here, we systematically benchmark 11 model configurations across five experimental IR benchmarks derived from NIST gas-phase, liquid-phase, solid-phase, and pooled spectra, together with an independent Chemotion collection.

title: Performance and Limitations of a 3D-Printed, Camera-Based DIY Spectrophotometer for Analytical Chemistry Education
abstract: To assess the analytical capabilities and educational potential of accessible instrumentation, we evaluated a 3D-printed, camera-based do-it-yourself (DIY) spectrophotometer. Wavelength mapping employed four reference light sources spanning 365-650 nm, and sodium copper chlorophyllin response was assessed at ten concentrations from 3 to 30 ppm, with three replicates per concentration. Spectra of five aqueous chromophoric samples were also compared with measurements from a commercial UV-Visible spectrophotometer.

title: Convergence and Precision of Harmonic Free Energies in Molecular Crystals
abstract: The thermodynamic properties of molecular crystals are commonly calculated at the harmonic level. Despite being the simplest approach to incorporating vibrational effects, their calculation is expensive and fraught with difficulties. The presence of a divergence in the entropy integrand at zero frequency in combination with artifacts from the usually employed Fourier interpolation and noise in the DFT forces make finite-displacement calculations difficult to converge to an acceptable precision. There are two objectives to this work.

title: Influence of Roughness on Sum Frequency Generation from Naphthalenetetracarboxylic Dianhydride Thin Films
abstract: Naphthalenetetracarboxylic dianhydride (NTCDA) films were characterized by AFM and found to exhibit Volmer-Weber growth where films form as islands with bare substrate between them. Polarization-dependent vibrational sum frequency generation (VSFG) spectroscopy was then performed on a range of film thicknesses to determine structural differences and similarities at the substrate and air interfaces.

title: Theory and chemical applications of the ψk-index of graphs
abstract: For an integer k ≥ 1, the k-th distance degree d_k(v) of a vertex v is the number of vertices at distance exactly k from v. We introduce the ψk-index, Ψk(G) = Σ_{uv∈E(G)} (d_k(u)+1)(d_k(v)+1)/(d_k(u)+d_k(v)+2), a bond-additive descriptor that is defined for every graph, including graphs with vertices of zero k-distance degree, and that is generated from the ψk-polynomial by a single differential operator.

title: Oxidation and temperature limits of sharp ZrB2–SiC nose tips in hypersonic flight: a coupled screening model
abstract: Sharp-edge flight envelopes consider temperature alone, yet sharp ZrB2–SiC nose tips can also fail by losing their protective borosilicate glass or by SiC active oxidation. We couple stagnation-point heating, conduction and a layered oxidation model to map the Mach numbers and altitudes at which a tip lasts 30 minutes. Four mechanistic findings come from comparing runs of the same model, so they depend less on its absolute accuracy than the maps do.

title: Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning for Sample Efficient Experimentation
abstract: Self-driving laboratories must learn to control a process from tens to hundreds of expensive experiments, too few for deep reinforcement learning (RL). We learn the Q-function directly with a Gaussian process (GP), which avoids learning the dynamics, and show that the GP posterior supplies the learning rate of Q-learning. If each Bellman target is treated as a noisy measurement of the Q-function, the learning rate that minimises the mean squared error is the Kalman gain, and applying it to every observed transition is equivalent to GP regression. Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning (HGPQ) sets the noise variance of each target with a heteroscedastic GP, which learns how unreliable the targets are across the states and inputs. Targets from noisy operating conditions, or from regions where the value function has large gradients, then move the estimate less than targets from low-noise regions, so HGPQ learns quickly where the data are reliable without being misled where they are not. For kernel value iteration with per-target variances that are assigned when a target is collected, we prove a high-probability bound on the error of the value estimate, uniform over the explored region. Pooled over five simulated benchmarks, which include a chemical reactor and a bioprocess, HGPQ approaches the best return found by any method in fewer episodes than GP, kernel and deep RL baselines.

title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
abstract: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
abstract: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

title: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
abstract: Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: CAE-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Reusable CAE Solver Development
abstract: We developed CAE-Bench, a benchmark to evaluate AI agents on Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) solver development. A CAE solver is more than a PDE solver; it must be able to generalize across various inputs, such as different boundary conditions, geometries, and material properties. CAE-Bench evaluates the generalizability of AI-developed CAE solvers by providing the same task, such as a heat transfer problem, multiple cases, with each case specifying an input. The AI agent develops a solver for a fixed task using only a few public cases, and the resulting solver is then tested on held-out cases, i.e., cases it has never seen before. We evaluate 12 models across a range of reasoning settings on 80 computational tasks. Our experiments show that even if a solver developed by an AI agent performs well on the public cases, it may even get 0 score on held-out cases. For tasks such as fluid dynamics problems, even the solver developed by GPT-6 Astra performs poorly on held-out cases. A data format and an SDK for task registration are provided, so the researcher can use the benchmark on their own infrastructure. We hope that CAE-Bench will help the community to develop AI agents that can develop reusable CAE solvers that generalize to various inputs.

title: Moiré Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
abstract: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moiré Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling ν_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moiré Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
abstract: The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
abstract: Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Microkinetic Modelling of Photocatalytic Water Splitting With Coupled Light Intensity and Temperature Effects
abstract: This work establishes a density functional theory (DFT)-informed microkinetic model to describe light-driven water splitting as a function of temperature and light intensity by integrating DFT calculations with experimental validation. Using Rh/Cr2O3-CoOOH/Al:SrTiO3 as a representative photocatalytic system, the model captures the surface kinetics of water oxidation on the CoOOH (110) cocatalyst surface, while proton reduction and the subsequent recombination of hydrogen radicals are assumed to occur on the Rh cocatalyst. The proposed reaction mechanism exhibits low activation barriers of 0.13 and 0.06 eV for water splitting steps 1 and 3, respectively. Step 2 has a moderate activation barrier of 0.27 eV. In contrast, step 4 is kinetically less favorable and requires a rearrangement of O* and OH·* surface species, exhibiting a Gibbs free energy barrier of 0.93 eV. The formed O2 desorbs from the surface with an activation barrier of 0.73 eV. The microkinetic model incorporating DFT-derived energies showed good agreement with experimental hydrogen production data. Surface coverages of 2H2O* and OH·* were found to be inversely proportional under all investigated reaction conditions. H2 production rates increase with both light intensity and temperature. Degree of rate control analysis revealed that the elementary steps involving the photogenerated charge carriers control the overall rate of the process. These findings represent a microkinetic description of the photocatalytic water splitting mechanism that explicitly incorporates the coupled effects of temperature and light intensity, offering mechanistic insights into the interplay between charge-carrier dynamics and surface reaction kinetics.

title: Heteronuclear Ru–Fe Dual Single-Atom Sites Anchored on Lanthanum Metal–Organic Framework Catalyzing the Base-Free Selective Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
abstract: Heteronuclear dual-single-atom catalysts featuring tailorable electronic structures and cooperative dual-site functionalities have received significant attention. However, their applications in the complex selective conversion of biomass molecules are still scarce and challenging. Here, a lanthanum metal–organic framework (MOF)-anchored RuFe heteronuclear dual-single-atom catalyst (RuFe/LaMOF) was prepared.

title: Revealing the transcriptomic organization of extrasomatic interfaces using SCOUBI
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) generates substantial transcript signal outside segmented cell bodies, which is generally discarded by analysis tools. This is especially problematic for brain ST data, as neuronal mRNAs can be localized far from somata – in axons, dendrites, and synaptic compartments – and up to half of the transcripts in ST data may lie outside cell bodies. Here, we present SCOUBI, a computational framework that identifies axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in ST data, revealing a hitherto overlooked layer of molecular function in neural tissues.

title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$
abstract: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
abstract: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. Its QHI loop uses the observed response to update runtime dispatch, revise physical plans, and select experiments for later proposals. An independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement. With fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, the evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

title: Location-Dependent Phase Evolution of Nickel in Fe2O3@LaFeO3 Oxygen Carriers for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production
abstract: Fe2O3@LaFeO3 core@shell oxygen carriers with controlled Ni incorporation were investigated for chemical looping hydrogen production. The catalytic behavior strongly depended on the initial location of Ni, which led to distinct Ni-containing phases and different structural evolution during redox cycling. The shell-incorporated Ni carrier exhibited stable redox cycling over 100 cycles, whereas the Ni-free and core-incorporated Ni samples showed lower activity or gradual performance decline.

title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
abstract: Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
abstract: The drive toward heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet packages promises unmatched performance and customization, yet the resulting density amplifies thermal challenges. To facilitate rapid design space exploration, we present ThermLeT, a multimodal transformer-based, scale invariant surrogate that integrates power density maps, spatial coordinate embeddings, material properties and heat transfer rate to predict steady state temperature in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than conventional finite element solvers such as ANSYS. To train the transformer model, we also create a dataset of 6,221 chiplet layouts perturbed from three representative architectures. On a 150 sample test set, ThermLeT achieves an RMSE of 3.16°C and an MAE of 2.24°C, improving accuracy by 35% over ThermEDGe and by 71% over HotSpot, while running approximately 6x and 11x lower inference latencies respectively. Ablation studies confirm robust generalization to unseen floorplans. Code and dataset available at https://github.com/MicroSystemsDesignLab/ThermLeT

title: Scaling a Universal Graph Neural Network Force Field to Billions of Atoms on Desk-Side GPUs
abstract: Machine-learning force fields are capable of simulating billions of atoms, but usually require high-performance supercomputing clusters. We show that a universal graph neural network force field, ALIGNN-FF, evaluates energies and forces of more than one billion atoms on desk-side computers such as the NVIDIA GB10, which has 128 GB of unified memory, by using a cube-and-halo decomposition. The halo contains every atom within the model's 20 Å receptive field, which makes the result exact. One GB10 holds 216,000 atoms with forces as a single graph. The cube-and-halo decomposition removes this limit, enabling an evaluation of 2 billion atoms on nine GB10s. We also demonstrate three case studies: a billion-atom polycrystal, a 102-million-atom microelectronic gate stack and a 1.07-million-atom satellite tobacco mosaic virus in water. This brings single-point evaluations at experimentally relevant sizes within reach of one research group. The code is available at: https://github.com/atomgptlab/scalingmat.

title: GPRidge: Gaussian-process Accelerated Calculations of Minimum Energy Paths and First-order Saddle Points
abstract: GPRidge, a Gaussian-process (GP) library for accelerating calculations of minimum energy paths and first-order saddle points with compiled-language and Python bindings, is presented. An evaluation controller uses GP predictions to iteratively adjust the Cartesian coordinates of the atoms. The fitted GP energy surface and measured energies and forces pass from the path calculation to local refinement of the saddle point. New evaluations improve the surrogate and check the candidate geometry. For the molecular calculations, acceptance requires measured-force convergence and an independent Hessian with only one negative eigenvalue. A second negative eigenvalue triggers an escape and renewed refinement. The controller supports a joint inverse-distance GP for molecules and local GP residuals on periodic systems. Applications to the 24 Baker-Chan and 20 Birkholz-Schlegel molecular reactions using the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA-S-1.1), and to 72 Pt heptamer and island rearrangements on Pt(111) using a Morse potential, are presented. On matched Baker-Chan reactions, GPRidge uses 7.8- and 7.0-fold fewer energy-and-force evaluations than climbing-image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) and off-path climbing-image nudged elastic band (OCI-NEB), respectively, reducing validation-inclusive CI-NEB time by 41%. All 20 Birkholz-Schlegel saddle points pass the independent index-one check, compared with 17 for the classical dimer method started from the same path maxima; on those 17 reactions, the GP dimer stage uses 6.4-fold fewer evaluations. All 72 Pt(111) paths meet the OptBench force criterion, with median evaluation counts of 30 and 23 for the heptamer and island problems, against 778 and 443 for CI-NEB.

Probing Phase Fluctuations in Cuprates by Multidimensional Josephson Spectroscopy
abstract: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.

title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, and models state almost the same confidence on tasks they get wrong as on tasks they get right. We also post-train Qwen3.5-9B with LoRA and reinforcement learning, rewarded by the share of answer criteria the simulation results confirm; on the held-out test split its score rises from 0.071 to 0.106. We release the train, validation and test splits, the evaluation harness and the leaderboard.

title: Multicomponent Adaptive Sampling Configuration Interaction method in openLOWDIN: positronic and quantum nuclear systems
abstract: We present a multicomponent Selective Configuration Interaction (SCI) method based on the deterministic Adaptive Sampling CI (ASCI) algorithm for computing energies and wavefunction properties of molecular systems containing leptons of variable masses, or quantum nuclei. Near-FCI accuracy is achieved by incorporating second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory or by dressing the Hamiltonian via Davidson's and co-workers shifted-Bk method. We validate the approach through benchmark positronic (e$^+$LiH, e$^+$OH$^-$, e$^+$Mg) and quantum nuclear systems (HCN), establishing a novel protocol for accurate convergence, based on the iterative adaptation of natural orbitals starting from those obtained by considering only cross-particle CISD excitations, to those obtained from SCI variational space, surpassing the accuracy of previous SCI studies. Overall, we show that the present multi-component SCI framework offers a simple, systematically improvable, and cost-effective alternative to traditional CI approaches.

title: Correlative Multidimensional Tracking and Modeling Reveals Mechanical Regulation of Nanoparticle Endocytosis
abstract: Understanding nanoparticle–membrane interactions during endocytosis is critical for advancing nanomedicine. However, a comprehensive understanding of its dynamic complexity remains elusive, largely due to limitations in often oversimplified theoretical models and experimental challenges in correlating nanoparticle conformations and protein assemblies. To bridge this persistent theoretical–experimental divide, we developed an integrated approach combining multidimensional single-particle tracking with theoretical modeling for understanding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of rod-shaped…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed band-gap variation. Furthermore, first-principles phonon calculations for the optimized crystal structure revealed peaks in the phonon density of states near these two characteristic energies. These results suggest that electron-phonon interactions play an important role in the anomalous temperature dependence of the optical band gap in TiNCl, with low- and higher-energy phonons contributing to the low-temperature decrease and the higher-temperature increase, respectively.

title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $Γ$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. We further show that external vertical electric fields, twist engineering, and both out-of-plane and in-plane strain provide efficient means to tune the band alignment, charge transfer, and Rashba parameters. In particular, electric fields and mechanical strain can drive reversible transitions between type-II and type-III band alignments while simultaneously modifying the Rashba spin texture and the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) window. The twisted heterostructure with $θ= 21.79^\circ$ exhibits similar tunability, including strain-induced transitions between distinct band-alignment regimes. These findings establish MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs as versatile multifunctional platforms combining electrically tunable Rashba spin splitting with controllable type-II/type-III band alignment, offering promising opportunities for next-generation TFETs and spintronic devices.

title: Separating learning from search and feedback in budgeted inverse design of periodic unit cells
abstract: To design a periodic material, engineers choose the shape and dimensions of a repeating cell to meet target properties. With few simulations, the benefit of a learned predictor can be hard to separate from the effect of which designs the search tries and how it uses simulator feedback. We compare two ways to predict properties in a library of 80 cell architectures, with up to 30 simulator calls per target. For each architecture, both searches use a table of predicted properties at different dimensions. One fills the table with predictions from neural networks. The other fits a simple model to the existing simulations for that architecture. Both searches use the difference between the predicted and simulated properties to adjust the next design. We generated 200 targets from simulated designs after fixing the analysis plan. The two searches showed no detectable difference in how often they matched all three properties within 2% or in the mean error of their returned designs. The upper limit of the 95% confidence interval for the gain in overall success rate was 4.5 percentage points. Follow-up controls on these targets changed success from 83.5% to 36.0% with a degraded table and 96.5% with an oracle table. In separate tests, using the simulation result to adjust the next design increased success for both types of table. Results cover one library and a coarse 32^3 voxel simulator. Designers can use this comparison to judge what a learned predictor adds when the search, feedback and budget are the same.

title: Long-Acting GLP-1 Receptor Agonism Ameliorates Sinoatrial Node Dysfunction by Attenuating Electrophysiological and Structural Remodeling
abstract: Background: Sinoatrial node dysfunction (SND) causes bradyarrhythmia, while pacemaker therapy does not reverse injury to the sinoatrial node (SAN). Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) raise heart rate, but whether they can repair an injured SAN in SND remains unknown. Methods: In streptozotocin-induced SND rats, we studied an acute phase (SND, GLP-1RA treatment, glycemic control, and GLP-1R antagonist groups) and a chronic phase (SND, GLP-1RA treatment, and glycemic control groups).

title: Ion selectivity as a biophysical determinant of action-potential dynamics
abstract: Ion selectivity is a fundamental property of voltage-gated ion channels, yet its contribution to action-potential dynamics has received less attention than channel conductance and gating kinetics. Here, we investigate how Na+/K+ permeability ratios influence membrane excitability, extending a multiscale framework that connects molecular properties of ion channels to neuronal electrical activity. We employ a simplified membrane depolarization model and a modified Hodgkin-Huxley model in which channel reversal potentials are determined by the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation, allowing selectivity to be varied independently of conductance and gating. We find that decreasing Nav selectivity reduces the inward driving force, slowing the action-potential upstroke and lowering its peak amplitude. This dependence is nonlinear: action-potential amplitude is more sensitive to changes at lower Nav selectivity and approaches a plateau as selectivity increases. Reduced Kv selectivity has qualitatively different consequences, shifting the equilibrium membrane potential toward more positive values and producing distinct dynamical regimes, including spontaneous firing and sustained depolarization with suppressed firing. Changes in Nav conductance affect action-potential dynamics through a distinct mechanism. Together, these results identify ion selectivity as an independent biophysical determinant of neuronal excitability and establish a quantitative connection between pore-level permeability and cellular electrical behavior. This approach provides a basis for incorporating molecular changes in ion selectivity into multiscale models of neuronal signaling.
